# wso2is_claim (Resource)

Manages a local claim. A local claim is a user attribute in the `http://wso2.org/claims` dialect. The resource also sets where each user store keeps the attribute.

Applications do not see local claims directly. To send the attribute to applications, map it in the OIDC dialect with `wso2is_external_claim` (`dialect_uri = "http://wso2.org/oidc/claim"`), and add it to an OIDC scope with `wso2is_oidc_scope`. To show it in the SCIM APIs, map it in a SCIM dialect too. To import a claim, use its claim URI.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "wso2is_claim" "employee_id" {
  claim_uri            = "http://wso2.org/claims/employeeId"
  display_name         = "Employee ID"
  description          = "HR employee number"
  regex                = "^E[0-9]{5}$"
  supported_by_default = true
  attribute_mappings = {
    PRIMARY = "employeeId"
  }
}

# Expose it in SCIM and in OIDC tokens.
resource "wso2is_external_claim" "employee_id_scim" {
  dialect_uri            = "urn:scim:schemas:extension:custom:User"
  claim_uri              = "urn:scim:schemas:extension:custom:User:employeeId"
  mapped_local_claim_uri = wso2is_claim.employee_id.claim_uri
}

resource "wso2is_external_claim" "employee_id_oidc" {
  dialect_uri            = "http://wso2.org/oidc/claim"
  claim_uri              = "employee_id"
  mapped_local_claim_uri = wso2is_claim.employee_id.claim_uri
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `attribute_mappings` (Map of String) User store attribute (column or LDAP attribute) by user store domain, for example `{ PRIMARY = "employeeId" }`.
- `claim_uri` (String) Claim URI, for example `http://wso2.org/claims/employeeId`. Changing it replaces the claim.
- `display_name` (String) Name shown in forms and the Console.

### Optional

- `canonical_values` (Attributes List) Allowed values (shown as a drop-down). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--canonical_values))
- `data_type` (String) `string`, `boolean`, `integer`, `decimal`, `date_time` or `complex`. The default is `string`.
- `description` (String) Description.
- `display_order` (Number) Position of the attribute in profile and registration forms. The default is `0`.
- `excluded_user_stores` (Set of String) User stores where the attribute is not available.
- `input_type` (String) Input control used in forms, for example `text_input`, `dropdown`, `checkbox_group`, `radio_group`, `date_picker`, `toggle`.
- `managed_in_user_store` (Boolean) Whether the value is stored in the user store (otherwise in the identity database).
- `multi_valued` (Boolean) The attribute holds several values. The default is `false`.
- `profiles` (Attributes Map) Per-profile overrides (WSO2 IS 7.1+), keyed by profile: `console`, `endUser`, `selfRegistration`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--profiles))
- `properties` (Map of String) Additional claim properties. Only the keys listed here are managed.
- `read_only` (Boolean) Users cannot change the value. The default is `false`.
- `regex` (String) Regular expression values must match.
- `required` (Boolean) A value is mandatory in profiles. The default is `false`.
- `shared_profile_value_resolving_method` (String) How the value is resolved for users shared with sub-organizations: `FromOrigin`, `FromSharedProfile` or `FromFirstFoundInHierarchy`.
- `sub_attributes` (List of String) Sub-attribute claim URIs of a `complex` attribute.
- `supported_by_default` (Boolean) Shown in user profiles (and self registration) by default. The default is `false`.
- `uniqueness_scope` (String) Uniqueness validation: `NONE`, `WITHIN_USERSTORE` or `ACROSS_USERSTORES`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Claim ID (base64url of the claim URI).

<a id="nestedatt--canonical_values"></a>
### Nested Schema for `canonical_values`

Required:

- `label` (String) Display label.
- `value` (String) Stored value.


<a id="nestedatt--profiles"></a>
### Nested Schema for `profiles`

Optional:

- `read_only` (Boolean) Users cannot change the value in this profile.
- `required` (Boolean) Required in this profile.
- `supported_by_default` (Boolean) Shown in this profile.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import wso2is_claim.employee_id http://wso2.org/claims/employeeId
```
